chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said:
The 'Aqiqah is obligatory when a man has a child; if he wishes to name it on the day it is born, he may do so.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqiqah, ritual sacrifice of an animal upon the birth of a child
key_terms.وَاجِبَةٌ: Obligatory (a specific category of legal ruling in Shia fiqh)

ai.seo_question: Is Aqiqah obligatory in Shia Islam and when should it be performed?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the 'Aqiqah as obligatory (wajib) upon the birth of a child, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus on this act of gratitude. It further links the ritual to the immediate naming of the child, emphasizing the father's role in establishing the child's identity and spiritual status from the very first day of life.
